items.example: The hotel was clean. However, the rooms were very noisy.

note.en: Starts a new sentence. Put a comma after it.
note.es: Empieza una frase nueva. Lleva coma detrás.

items.example: Living near the station is convenient. On the other hand, it can be noisy at night.

note.en: Needs an 'on the one hand' idea, or at least a first idea, before it.
note.es: Necesita una primera idea antes («on the one hand» o similar).

items.example: Although the course is expensive, it is worth the money.

note.en: Do not add 'but' in the second part.
note.es: No añadas «but» en la segunda parte.

items.example: The film was too long. Still, I enjoyed it.
The train was delayed. Even so, we arrived before the meeting started.
Prices have risen sharply. Despite this, the shop is as busy as ever.

note.en: 'Despite' is followed by a noun or -ing form, never by a clause.
note.es: «Despite» va con sustantivo o -ing, no con una oración.

items.example: Most city dwellers rely on buses, whereas people in the countryside need a car.

note.en: Compares two different groups or situations.
note.es: Compara dos grupos o situaciones distintas.

items.example: I don't enjoy early starts. That said, the quiet mornings in the office are useful.
The results were disappointing. Nevertheless, the team decided to continue the project.
Notwithstanding the budget cuts, the library has extended its opening hours.

note.en: Very formal; followed by a noun phrase.
note.es: Muy formal; va seguido de un sintagma nominal.

items.example: Having said that, I would not turn down a job offer from a competitor.
Online sales grew steadily. By contrast, in-store sales fell for the third year.

note.en: Compares two clear opposites, often with figures.
note.es: Compara dos opuestos claros, a menudo con datos.

items.example: I like tea, but I don't like coffee.
The hotel is cheap. But it is far from the beach.
